skill.name: fingerprint-failure-triage
skill.description: Analyze a liarjs fingerprint report and attribute each failing check to the launch configuration, page-modifying layer, network path, or machine image. Explain which failures are expected in headless or datacenter environments.
skill.summary: Attribute liarjs fingerprint failures to the component that produced each signal.
skill.author: liarjsdev

content.value_statement: Low fingerprint scores do not show which browser layer caused each contradiction. This skill groups failing checks by owner and identifies failures that are expected in headless or datacenter environments.
actual_capabilities: Groups failing liarjs checks by launch configuration, page modification, network path, or machine image.
Explains what common checks measure, including webdriver, native-integrity, worker-consistency, gpu-triad, and tz.
Uses passing checks to distinguish between competing sources for a failure.
Identifies failures that are expected from headless browsers, proxies, datacenter IPs, or virtual machines.
Compares before and after scan results when the operator provides both reports.
limitations: It interprets supplied reports and does not run a fingerprint scan by itself.
It does not predict how a website will evaluate an IP, account, or browsing behavior.
It does not prescribe browser configuration changes for every use case.
Its command examples require the operator to review and trust the package before execution.

use_cases.title: Investigate a low score
use_cases.description: Give the skill a complete liarjs report and receive an owner-based explanation of the failing checks.

use_cases.title: Review a proxy mismatch
use_cases.description: Use the network group to explain timezone, language, WebRTC, header, or edge-classification contradictions.

use_cases.title: Compare browser builds
use_cases.description: Provide before and after reports to identify which checks changed and which browser layer likely caused the movement.

prompt_templates.title: Explain this report
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this liarjs fingerprint report and explain each failing check in plain language. Group the checks by responsible component.

prompt_templates.title: Separate expected failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this report from a headless browser and label each failure as expected environment behavior or an inconsistency requiring investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Find the likely owner
prompt_templates.prompt: Attribute these failing check IDs to launch configuration, page modification, network path, or machine image. Use passing checks to resolve ambiguous ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two scans
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these before and after liarjs reports. List only checks whose status changed, group related changes, and identify the most likely changed component.

output_examples.input: A report shows failures for webdriver, headless-ua, and headless-viewport.
output_examples.output: These checks belong to the launch configuration. They indicate an automated headless browser presentation, so the failures are expected for a stock headless run.

output_examples.input: The report shows tz, lang, and ua-http-js failures, while browser APIs are internally consistent.
output_examples.output: These failures belong to the network path. The exit location, request headers, and JavaScript values disagree, so the proxy or header configuration is the likely owner.

output_examples.input: A before-and-after comparison shows native-integrity and worker-consistency changing together.
output_examples.output: The page-modifying layer is the likely owner. A change reached one JavaScript realm or altered function identity without producing a consistent result across realms.

best_practices: Provide the complete report, including passing checks, before asking for attribution.
Investigate one browser or network change at a time so results remain attributable.
Describe improved results as fewer contradictions, not as a guarantee of website acceptance.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a low score as proof that one browser setting caused every failure.
Do not infer website behavior from a local fingerprint report alone.
Do not apply configuration changes before identifying the component that owns the signal.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a complete liarjs fingerprint report with passing and failing checks. Two reports are useful for before-and-after comparisons.

faq.question: Does this skill run the scan?
faq.answer: No. It interprets reports. A separate scan must produce the report before triage begins.

faq.question: What does a headless failure mean?
faq.answer: Headless checks often describe the browser accurately. They can be expected environment signals rather than defects.

faq.question: Who owns timezone failures?
faq.answer: The network path usually owns tz failures because the exit IP location and browser timezone can be configured independently.

faq.question: Why compare passing checks?
faq.answer: Passing checks provide context that can distinguish a launch, page-modification, network, or machine-image cause.

faq.question: Can the score predict site access?
faq.answer: No. A local score measures internal coherence, not IP reputation, account history, or browsing behavior.
